# One-call coherent filtering: exact instrument, and a cheaper conventional realization
2026-10-29. New local derivation and numerical checks; established coherent-check mechanism, not a new generic quantum capability. Independent review pending.

## Decision
The proposed random m-branch filter is mathematically valid under the stated representation and isolated-control contracts. But for a completed k-qubit logical channel, **b=log2(m) ordinary random coherent Pauli checks plus one Pauli pad implement exactly the same accepted joint CP map with O(bk), rather than O(mk), controlled operations**. This defeats a generic advantage claim for the multiplexor. The useful retained result is a precisely scoped one-call, retained-memory erasure interface and the obligation to acquire reliable coherent flags. Clifford authentication is a second strong comparator, not an overlooked alternative.

## 1. Exact multibranch instrument
Let N have Kraus K_a:L⊗M→L⊗M', with arbitrary retained memory dimensions and arbitrary input/reference correlations. The opaque source acts on L,M only. A fresh b-qubit protected flag F is initialized to |u>=m^(-1/2)Σ_j|j>, m=2^b. Independently draw g_1,...,g_m from a unitary conjugation 1-design on L. No branch key or flag information is leaked through a side port, timing, or retained control record. The source may infer information from L itself; that is included in the same fixed conditional joint N.

Apply V=Σ_j |j><j|⊗U_gj before the one ordinary call and V† after it, then project F onto |u>. This needs no controlled N, environment access, inverse N, or source reset. Accepted Kraus:

A_a(g_1,...,g_m) = (1/m)Σ_j (U_gj†⊗I_M') K_a (U_gj⊗I_M).

Define K_ag by the summand, Kbar_a=E_g K_ag, T=E_g Σ_a K_ag(·)K_ag†, and G=Σ_a Kbar_a(·)Kbar_a†. Then B=T−G is CP: its Kraus covariance expression is E_g Σ_a(K_ag−Kbar_a)(·)(K_ag−Kbar_a)†. Expanding all m² terms and using independent keys gives EXACTLY

A_acc = G + B/m.                                          (1)

The equality is of complete CP maps, not just reduced states, therefore extends to all references and entangled LM inputs. # Receiving review: coherent multibranch filtering

2026-10-29. Accepted as an exact instrument with explicit ideal-control conditions, and as a useful negative comparison result. No generic historical novelty or advantage is accepted.

## Algebra and retained memory

Expanding the average of m independent conjugated Kraus operators gives diagonal terms T/m and off-diagonal terms (1−1/m)G. Therefore the accepted map is G+(T−G)/m. T−G has the explicit positive covariance-Kraus representation. This equality holds before tracing memory and extends to every reference. For the Pauli basis, averaging removes unequal components and leaves id⊗B0 plus weighted Pauli branches. The trace effect is scalar on the logical space, so the actual accepted memory map factors through the incoming memory marginal even when logical input and memory are correlated. The subnormalized half-diamond bound follows by comparing two CP maps with the same bad trace effect. No normalized bound is inferred without acceptance control.

For general irreducible group representations, Schur yields the same scalar memory effect. Even if one uses only a conjugation 1-design ensemble rather than a whole group, the marginal conclusion follows directly: trace removes the post-unitary, and the pre-unitary average replaces the logical input by I/d times its memory marginal. A covariance argument should not be read as automatically applying to every nongroup ensemble; this does not invalidate the stated group uses or the map identity.

The raw input/output intertwiner claim requires a genuine common group representation and multiplicity one. Extending projective Pauli representatives by identity on leakage violates that premise. The qutrit example gives acceptance 5/8 rather than 1/2; honest Q8 restores the result. Completing the logical decoder first is a different, valid interface with a different GOOD component. No N1041 control protection is inherited automatically.
